title: Delivery is complete but not billable
prompt: A delivery is complete and goods issue is posted, but the business cannot find it in the billing due list. Explain how you would diagnose the issue without forcing an invoice.
expected_points: Start with billing relevance, billing status, billing block, billing date, completion and already-billed state.
Confirm the exact reference document and item that should be billed.
Separate due-list selection/filtering from true billability.
Use document flow and status evidence before changing configuration.
Explain why manual billing can hide an upstream process defect.
follow_up_questions: What would you check if only one item of the delivery is missing from the due list?
How would a billing plan or partial billing change your diagnosis?
red_flags: Lists transaction codes without a hypothesis tree
Assumes goods issue alone guarantees billability

title: Unexpected invoice split
prompt: Two deliveries for the same customer and billing date create two invoices, while the business expected one collective invoice. Explain how you prove the split reason before proposing a fix.
expected_points: Treat billing as a convergence problem and compare split-relevant header values.
Use split analysis to identify the differing field instead of guessing.
Check payer/bill-to, currency, payment terms, sales organization, tax/VAT context and other split-relevant values.
Trace the differing value to its owner: master data, source document, copy logic or custom data transfer.
Challenge whether convergence is legally and financially valid before removing a split criterion.
follow_up_questions: What if the split is caused by different payment terms?
When would custom split logic be justified?
red_flags: Says same customer should always produce one invoice
Removes a split field without understanding its business meaning
Starts with custom code before split analysis

title: Order and invoice prices differ
prompt: The sales order shows a net value of 100 EUR, but the invoice shows 105 EUR. The business says Billing changed the price incorrectly. Trace the decision and explain when the difference can be expected.
expected_points: Check the billing pricing type in copying control before changing condition records.
Compare which price elements were copied, updated or redetermined.
Check billing date/context, scales, manual conditions, tax and other conditions that can legitimately change.
Separate source pricing correctness from billing transfer/redetermination behavior.
Prove the expected commercial value before deciding which layer is wrong.
follow_up_questions: How would pricing type C differ from a pure copy behavior?
What evidence would show that the pricing engine is correct but copying control is wrong?
red_flags: Assumes invoice must always equal sales-order value
Changes a condition record before checking pricing type
Mixes pricing transfer with revenue account determination

title: Correct invoice, wrong revenue account
prompt: The invoice amount and tax are correct, but the revenue is posted to the wrong G/L account. Explain how you separate commercial pricing from revenue account determination and prove the cause.
expected_points: Confirm that billing values are commercially correct before touching pricing.
Check billing posting status and the FI accounting document.
Trace account determination inputs such as chart of accounts, sales organization, customer/material account assignment groups, account key and relevant billing fields.
Identify the account key coming from the pricing procedure but keep account determination as a separate decision layer.
Prove the selected G/L account and correct the owning configuration or master-data input.
follow_up_questions: What if the accounting document was not created at all?
Which team owns the fix when the account key is correct but the account mapping is wrong?
red_flags: Changes price condition values to repair a G/L account
Stops at the billing document and ignores FI evidence
Says Finance owns everything after invoice creation

title: Billing is correct but e-invoice is rejected
prompt: The billing document and FI posting are correct, but the electronic invoice is rejected by the external compliance channel. Design a safe recovery path and explain system ownership.
expected_points: Keep the source billing document, FI state and eDocument/external transmission state as separate but connected layers.
Check eDocument type mapping, localization rules, generated representation, submission status and external response.
Decide whether the defect can be corrected or retried in the external-document layer without changing the commercial event.
Do not cancel a correct source invoice only because transport or format processing failed.
Respect country-specific legal rules before choosing cancellation or resubmission.
follow_up_questions: When would the source billing document itself need correction?
How would you make retries idempotent and auditable?
red_flags: Treats eDocument status as the same thing as FI posting status
Claims one universal correction process for all countries

title: Cancel, credit, or debit
prompt: An invoice was posted and sent to the customer, but the commercial amount is wrong. Compare cancellation and rebilling with a credit or debit correction. Explain what would change your decision.
expected_points: Separate reversal of the original billing event from a commercial adjustment to receivables.
Check original billing and FI state, customer receipt state, business reason and legal/localization constraints.
Use cancellation when the original invoice itself must be reversed and recreated, subject to process rules.
Use credit or debit correction when a controlled adjustment is the correct business event.
Preserve document flow, FI traceability and external invoice/eDocument status.
Explain that the correct choice is business and legal context dependent, not a preferred transaction code.
follow_up_questions: How would your answer change if the customer has not received the invoice yet?
What must be reconciled after a cancel-and-rebill path?
red_flags: Always cancels because it is simpler
Uses a manual compensating posting without reference discipline
